title: Phangan–Samui–Tao 5-Day Island Hopping Plan 2026 | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A real 5-day island hopping plan across Koh Phangan, Koh Samui and Koh Tao in Thailand's Gulf — with Lomprayah & Songserm ferry times, real ticket prices, piers and a day-by-day timeline.
keywords: Koh Phangan travel, island hopping Phangan Samui Tao, Gulf of Thailand ferry, three island Thailand itinerary, Koh Nang Yuan
intro: Three islands sit close together in the Gulf of Thailand, just an hour's boat ride apart, yet each has its own character. Koh Samui is the all-rounder with an airport you can fly straight into, Koh Phangan mixes party island with a chilled-out yoga crowd, and Koh Tao is a paradise for divers. This plan strings all three together as a 5-day, 4-night island hopping trip, with real ferry schedules, real ticket prices and the exact piers you'll land at. We'll be honest about the costs too, including how room rates spike around full moon nights.

blocks.html: If you've got around five days on the islands, sticking to just one feels like a missed chance, because Phangan, Samui and Tao all sit in the same cluster in the Gulf of Thailand. Speedboats between them take anywhere from 20 minutes to an hour and a half. You can buy tickets at the pier or book online ahead of time. This plan starts on Samui (since it has direct flights), then works its way out to Phangan and Tao before looping back, paced to match the ferry timetables each day.

blocks.text: Get to know the island ferries first

blocks.html: The boats are the backbone of this trip. The main operators are Lomprayah (fast catamarans, the most punctual) and Songserm (a little cheaper, a little slower). Both run all three islands every day, several times a day. Seatran and Raja Ferry focus more on the Samui–Surat Thani route. Tickets are sold at the pier or can be booked online ahead of time through sites like 12Go.

items: Samui ↔ Phangan — the quickest hop, around 20–45 minutes, several runs a day, tickets roughly 300–400 THB. Lomprayah docks at Thong Sala pier on the Phangan side.
Phangan ↔ Tao — around 1 hour, landing at Mae Haad pier on Koh Tao. Tickets roughly 400–600 THB.
Samui ↔ Tao — the fastest is the Lomprayah at around 1 hour 45 minutes, twice a day, departing Nathon pier from around 10:30, last run around 16:00.
Piers on the Phangan side — most island ferries come in and out of Thong Sala, which is also the island's main town and market.

blocks.title: How to book ferry tickets without getting caught out
blocks.html: During high season (December–April) and around full moon nights, boats fill up fast, so book 1–2 days ahead. Some operators include hotel pickup to the pier in the ticket. If you get seasick easily, pick a seat in the middle of the lower deck and take motion-sickness tablets 30 minutes before boarding.

blocks.title: Book the activities in your Koh Phangan trip ahead
blocks.text: Booking online ahead on Klook or GetYourGuide is usually cheaper than the gate and skips the queue. Pick only the experiences you actually want — prices and availability are shown live on each site.

blocks.text: Days 1–2 · Koh Samui, settle in before you set off

blocks.html: Start on Samui because you can fly straight in. It's the island that has everything ready to go — restaurants, hospitals and several different vibes all on one island. Use the first two days to get into the island rhythm, then hop across to Phangan.

items.activity: Land at Samui Airport, check in near Chaweng or Bophut
items.note: Chaweng is lively with lots of restaurants; Bophut is quieter and close to the fishing village.

items.activity: Relax on Chaweng Beach, swim, stroll along the shore
items.note: Long beach, white sand, but the evening crowds get heavy and the touts can be pretty pushy.

items.activity: Head up to the Big Buddha and watch the sunset
items.note: It's on the north of the island, near the airport. Dress modestly inside the temple grounds.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Bophut Fisherman's Village · pack up before the crossing

items.activity: Wake up slowly, coffee on Bophut beach
Visit a waterfall or viewpoint around the island, such as Na Muang Waterfall
items.note: Renting a motorbike is the easiest way around, but some roads are steep and slippery, so ride slowly.
If it lands on a Friday, there's the Walking Street, the island's biggest night market, 17:00–23:00.

items.activity: Pack your bags, check tomorrow morning's ferry to Phangan
items.note: The Samui–Phangan boat takes just 20–45 minutes. Book a late-morning run so you're not rushing.

blocks.text: Day 3 · Cross over to Koh Phangan

blocks.html: Take the boat from Samui over to Thong Sala pier — under an hour. Phangan has two sides on one island: Haad Rin is the party town and the birthplace of the Full Moon Party, while the north and west are the chilled side, all yoga and wellness cafes. Pick your accommodation based on which one you are.

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: Arrive on Phangan · Thong Sala–Haad Rin

items.activity: Boat arrives at Thong Sala pier, check in
items.note: Thong Sala is the main town with a market and convenience stores, and it's easy to get around from here.

items.activity: Head to Haad Rin, swim at the pretty curved sandy beach
items.note: The road from Thong Sala to Haad Rin is very steep. If you're not confident on a motorbike, take a songthaew instead.

items.activity: Catch the sunset on the west coast, such as Srithanu Beach
If it's a full moon night, head into the Haad Rin party, 200 THB entry
items.note: If it's not a full moon night, Haad Rin still has beachfront bars open every night, just a mellower scene.

blocks.title: Stay safe on Phangan (read this first)
blocks.html: If you're set on the Full Moon Party, check the dates carefully before booking tickets. In 2026 they fall on 29 Jun · 31 Jul · 28 Aug · 26 Sep · 27 Oct · 24 Nov · 24 Dec (dates may shift if they clash with Buddhist holy days). Drink responsibly and be wary of drinks you didn't see mixed. Leave valuables in your hotel safe and carry only the cash you need. Don't mess with the fire shows or fire skipping ropes while drunk — accidents happen every year. The sea is rough at night, so don't go swimming late.

blocks.text: Day 4 · Ferry on to Koh Tao, dive at Koh Nang Yuan

blocks.html: From Phangan it's about an hour's boat ride on to Koh Tao, landing at Mae Haad. Koh Tao is a magnet for divers from all over the world — clear water, plenty of coral, and one of the cheapest places to learn to dive. The one spot you can't skip is Koh Nang Yuan, three little islands joined by a sandbar, with a viewpoint so good it's become the postcard image of Koh Tao.

blocks.label: Day 4
blocks.title: Arrive on Tao · snorkel tour around the island

items.activity: Boat from Phangan arrives at Mae Haad, drop bags near Sairee Beach
items.note: Sairee is the main area with the most restaurants and dive shops.

items.activity: Join a snorkel tour around the island + Koh Nang Yuan
items.note: Half-day tours start around 500–890 THB/person · there's an extra 250 THB/person entry fee for Koh Nang Yuan, paid on the island.

items.activity: Climb the Koh Nang Yuan viewpoint, photograph the three-island sandbar
items.note: The path up is rocky with steps, so wear shoes with good grip.

items.activity: Back to Sairee Beach for the seaside sunset
items.note: Sairee faces west, so the sunset is good there every evening.

blocks.title: Dive safely
blocks.html: If you've never done scuba, start with a Discover Scuba session with an instructor for every one or two divers. Even when snorkelling, wear a life vest if you're not a strong swimmer. Check the weather before getting on the boat — during the monsoon (roughly Oct–Dec) the swell picks up and tours may be cancelled. Never touch or stand on the coral.

blocks.text: Day 5 · Loop back and head out

blocks.html: Plan the last day around your return flight. If you're flying out of Samui, allow for the Tao–Samui boat at around 1 hour 45 minutes, then the transfer to the airport. Morning boats usually leave Tao around 10:30. Double-check the latest schedule with the ferry company before your travel day.

items.activity: Pack up, breakfast on Sairee Beach
Take the Tao–Samui boat (Lomprayah, around 1 hr 45 min)
items.note: Land at Nathon pier on Samui, then it's about a 30–40 minute transfer to the airport.

items.activity: Allow time to check in at Samui Airport, fly home
items.note: If your flight is late, grab lunch around Nathon or Chaweng first.

items: Three ferry hops — Samui→Phangan→Tao→Samui comes to around 1,100–1,600 THB depending on the operator and season.

4 nights' accommodation — guesthouses from around 500–900 THB/night · mid-range resorts 1,500–3,000 THB/night · full moon nights on Phangan push prices up and often require a multi-night minimum stay.
Koh Tao diving tour — 500–890 THB + 250 THB Koh Nang Yuan entry fee.
Motorbike rental — around 200–300 THB/day + fuel (always photograph the bike before you take it, to avoid bogus damage charges).
Food — local spots run 60–150 THB a meal · beachfront tourist restaurants cost roughly twice as much.

blocks.title: Being honest about room rates around full moon
blocks.html: Room rates on Phangan swing hard with the season and full moon nights. Around full moon some places double their prices and enforce a 3–5 night minimum stay. If you're on a budget and not there for the party, going on weekdays is far better value, or stay on Samui/Tao and just take the boat over for the party night itself.

faq.q: Which island should you start with on a Phangan, Samui, Tao trip?
faq.a: Most people start on Samui because it has direct flights, then take the boat out to Phangan and Tao before looping back to fly home from Samui. If you fly into Surat Thani and connect by boat, you can just as easily start on Phangan or Tao.

faq.q: How long do the ferries between the three islands take?
faq.a: Samui–Phangan is the quickest at around 20–45 minutes, Phangan–Tao is about 1 hour, and Samui–Tao on the fast Lomprayah is around 1 hour 45 minutes. Every route runs several times a day. Book ahead during high season.

faq.q: Is 5 days enough to do all three islands?
faq.a: It's just about right — enough to get a feel for each island's character: two days on Samui, one on Phangan, one on Tao, and a travel day at the end. If you want to do serious diving or really go all in on the Full Moon Party, bump it up to 6–7 days.

faq.q: Do you have to come on a full moon night to enjoy it?
faq.a: Not at all. Phangan has plenty of charm on the chilled side too — quiet beaches up north, cafes and yoga. The Full Moon Party is just one night. If you don't like crowds or you're on a budget, skipping the full moon makes for an easier trip and much cheaper rooms.

faq.q: How much is the Koh Nang Yuan entry fee?
faq.a: The Koh Nang Yuan entry fee is around 250 THB per person, usually paid separately when you arrive on the island. Some tours include it in the package, so ask clearly before you book.
